source_title: Algebraic Approaches for the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem over Prime Fields

review_provenance.method: Independent review packet followed by direct primary-source confirmation.
review_provenance.boundary: The record binds claim locations and paraphrases. The paper leaves asymptotic complexity open and its experiments do not establish an advantage over generic algorithms.

claims.paraphrase: The first construction requires a B-smooth divisor of p-1 with size approximately p^(1/m), uses its multiplicative subgroup or a coset as the root set of a composed map, and inserts those constraints into the Semaev relation system.
claims.boundary: Raw factor-base size is only an applicability condition. Solver, recovery, relation collection, linear algebra, and preprocessing remain part of the total cost.

claims.paraphrase: For an arbitrary base-field prime, the second construction searches for an auxiliary curve over the same field whose order contains a B-smooth factor of size approximately p^(1/m). A self-isogeny of that auxiliary curve defines the composed root map used for the original target curve's factor-base coordinates.
claims.boundary: The auxiliary curve is not required to be related to the target curve beyond sharing the field. Its search cost, map construction, generalized-root solving, recovery, and total attack cost must all be priced.
